get.summary:
`GET /tunnel` — read the tunnel's observed liveness and public host as a
single wire snapshot. Gated by [`Scoped<TunnelSettingsReader>`]: the read
lives behind the `wildflower/TunnelSettings.r` capability, so this handler
never touches the router state directly (a `403` on an under-scoped token).
Collected into the `OpenAPI` doc via `routes!` in the parent module, which
reads this `#[utoipa::path]`.

200.description: The tunnel's observed liveness and public host

InsufficientScopeBody.description:
Wire shape for a 403 — the caller authenticated, but their token doesn't cover
the scope(s) an operation requires. `missingScopes` names the scopes the
caller must additionally hold.

error.description: Always `"InsufficientScope"` — the discriminant a client switches on.

missingScopes.description: The rendered scopes the caller lacks.

TunnelStateResponse.description:
Tunnel state on the wire: the observed liveness and the public host.

# Liveness is verified, not optimistic

`status` is the real [`TunnelStatus`] FSM position. `servedOrigin`
resolves to `https://{publicHost}` **only** while `status == "verified"` —
i.e. after a `/health` probe through the public origin came back healthy —
and the supervisor re-probes, so it reverts to the loopback fallback if the
tunnel silently drops. `running` is the coarse "a supervisor is attempting"
view (`dialing`/`verified`/`unreachable`).
`dialAttempts` counts relay dials since the server started — a counter
climbing with a steady `error` flags a permanent misconfiguration. This is
the resolution of <https://github.com/Assessment-is/Wildflower/issues/184>.

publicHost.description:
The bare public host the relay serves the server at, from the server's
record.

status.description: The liveness FSM position — the authoritative state. See the type docs.

running.description:
`true` when a supervisor is attempting (`dialing`/`verified`/
`unreachable`). A derived view of `status`.

dialAttempts.description:
How many times the tunnel has tried to dial the relay since the server
started. Surfaced so an operator can spot a permanent misconfiguration
(counter climbs with no recovery) without the daemon having to classify
rathole errors itself.

servedOrigin.description:
`https://{publicHost}` only while `status == "verified"`, else the
loopback fallback. See the type-level docs.

TunnelStatus.description:
The liveness state of the tunnel. The full FSM lives in the tunnel slice;
this is the position consumers care about.

This is also the type the tunnel slice's `/tunnel` HTTP surface serializes
directly (lowercase variants), so it derives `Serialize`/`ToSchema` here
rather than a parallel wire enum re-declaring the same variants.
